seo.title: Watercolor Botanical Wedding Invitation Maker – Printable
seo.description: Make a watercolor botanical wedding invitation with greenery and white florals. Add your names, date and venue, then download a 5×7 in print PDF with bleed.

intro: The watercolor botanical style frames your wedding details with delicate greenery and white flowers in a soft sage and ivory palette. The names are set in elegant script and the details in a refined serif, which gives the card a fresh, natural and slightly romantic feel.

Type in the couple's names, the date and the venue, and PiCraft sets them into the design with a balanced, centered layout. You download a 5×7 inch print PDF with bleed, a 300 DPI JPG and a phone-sized image for digital sharing.

bestFor.title: Garden and greenhouse weddings
bestFor.description: Leaves and white blooms echo venues with glass roofs, lawns or conservatories, so the card previews the setting.

bestFor.title: Spring and summer ceremonies
bestFor.description: The light green and ivory palette reads as fresh, which fits weddings from late spring to early autumn.

bestFor.title: Couples who want classic without gold
bestFor.description: It is traditional in tone but calm in color, a good choice if metallic borders feel too formal.

designNotes.title: Check the script on the names
designNotes.description: Script lettering can make a long pair of names harder to read. Use first names or short forms, and proofread the spelling on the generated card.

designNotes.title: Use the venue line for the venue name only
designNotes.description: Put the venue name in the venue field and the town in the city field, so the layout stays balanced above the greenery.

designNotes.title: Pick uncoated or textured paper
designNotes.description: Matte, slightly textured stock suits the watercolor look. Glossy paper can make the pale greens look flat.

designNotes.title: Echo the greenery in the flowers
designNotes.description: White blooms, eucalyptus or ruscus at the ceremony tie the day back to the invitation without extra planning.

RSVP line: "Kindly reply by May 1 · sophiaandliam.com"
A destination wedding with city set to "Lake Como, Italy"

faq.q: Will the greenery cover my text?
faq.a: The design keeps all text well inside the card, with margins of at least 8% on every side, and frames it with the greenery. Proofread the result and generate again if a line looks crowded.

faq.q: Can I add a monogram or crest?
faq.a: No. The maker does not add monograms, photos or maps. You can add them in a design editor after you download the file.

faq.q: Is the wording editable?
faq.a: In part. You choose an opening line and an invitation line from short lists, in English. Use the RSVP line for extra words, such as a website or dress code.

faq.q: What size should I print?
faq.a: The card is 5×7 inches with a 0.125 inch bleed. See the [wedding invitation size guide](/sizes/wedding-invitation-size) for envelopes and paper.

seo.title: Modern Minimal Wedding Invitation Maker – Clean & Printable
seo.description: Make a modern minimal wedding invitation with white space, thin-line accents and an elegant serif. Download a 5×7 in print PDF with bleed or a share image.

intro: The modern minimal style is about restraint: generous white space, fine thin-line accents and a high-contrast serif in black ink on warm white. There are no florals and no ornament, so the names, the date and the place carry the whole card.
Enter your details and PiCraft sets them in a clean, centered layout. Because the design is simple, it prints crisply even on a basic printer and looks good as a phone image.

bestFor.title: City and gallery weddings
bestFor.description: Modern venues such as lofts, galleries and restaurants pair naturally with a card that looks like a gallery poster.

bestFor.title: Small, intimate celebrations
bestFor.description: A quiet design suits a short guest list where the invitation is more a note than a show.

bestFor.title: Couples who like to add their own touches
bestFor.description: A plain card gives you room to add a sticker, a ribbon or a wax seal by hand.

designNotes.title: Let the typography lead
designNotes.description: With no decoration, the choice of words matters more. Use a clean line for the venue and keep the city short.

designNotes.title: Use white or cream stock
designNotes.description: The card is designed on warm white. Printing on bright white paper changes the feel slightly, so test one copy.

designNotes.title: Keep optional lines optional
designNotes.description: Time, city and RSVP are optional. Leave out any you do not need, and the white space gets even more generous.

designNotes.title: Add texture in the paper
designNotes.description: A thick cotton or felt-textured stock adds richness that the flat design leaves out, and a print shop can often supply it.

faq.q: Is minimal too plain for a wedding?
faq.a: It is simple on purpose, which many couples want. If you would like more decoration, the [classic gold](/create/wedding-invitation-maker/classic) and [botanical](/create/wedding-invitation-maker/botanical) styles add ornament.

faq.q: Does the card include a leaf or icon?
faq.a: Some results include a small motif or a thin border, and some do not. The style keeps decoration minimal, and each generation is a little different.

faq.q: Can I print at home?
faq.a: Yes. The minimal look suits home printing because there are no large dark areas. Print the JPG at actual size on heavy stock and trim along the edge.

faq.q: How do I send it digitally?
faq.a: Download the 1080×1500 px share image and send it by message or email. Keep a printed copy for guests who prefer paper.
